name: Hydrolytic Dispersion Charge HDC-2 'Saltflat'
description: The HDC-2 is a two-stage chemical-explosive device designed for data infrastructure denial. The outer shell contains a conventional shaped charge that ruptures a pressurized inner reservoir filled with a superheated hydrolytic solution — a proprietary TESSERA CORPONATION compound that aggressively attacks organic polymers, fiber-optic cladding, and unshielded circuit substrates on contact. The blast itself is modest; the real damage is the dispersed chemical payload that coats surfaces in a 5-meter radius with a compound that continues reacting for up to 40 minutes after detonation.
specifications:
weight: 1.2 kg
dimensions: 14 cm x 8 cm cylindrical
blast radius: 5 m primary, 9 m chemical drift
chemical active duration: 35–45 minutes post-detonation
trigger modes: Remote detonation, Timer, Tamper-triggered
neutralization agent: TESSERA proprietary NeutraFlush compound (sold separately)
casing material: Corrosion-resistant ceramic-alloy shell
tactical_use: Deployed in corporate sabotage operations targeting server farms, communication hubs, and fabrication lines. Teams plant HDC-2 units inside conduit junctions or cable management systems where the chemical dispersal maximizes contact with sensitive infrastructure. Anti-personnel use is considered secondary — the hydrolytic compound causes severe chemical burns, but the weapon is rarely chosen for its human lethality. It is exceptionally effective at making a location digitally dead for hours.
cultural_context: The HDC-2 is the calling card of data-warfare crews and anti-corporate saboteurs in GLMZ. Finding one at a crime scene tells investigators less about who planted it and more about what the target was — if someone used a Saltflat, they wanted the data gone more than they wanted people dead. TESSERA markets a civilian variant for 'industrial equipment decommissioning,' which fools no one.
known_users: Insurance fraud operators targeting competitor facilities
story_hooks: A runner is hired to plant an HDC-2 in a competitor's server room, only to find the room already destroyed by an identical charge — someone got there first, and the data the runner was supposed to destroy is already gone.

A TESSERA 'decommissioning' team is found dead in an industrial district, their own HDC-2 units detonated around them. The chemical burns suggest the charges were triggered remotely — from inside TESSERA's own network.
The NeutraFlush neutralization compound has been pulled from the market without explanation, and three active HDC-2 sites in the city are now impossible to safely contain.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact cylindrical device with an aggressive, purposeful stance. The outer casing has a subtle bulge at its equator suggesting internal pressure containment. The overall impression is clinical and deliberate—something designed by engineers who prioritize function over aesthetics. No decorative elements; every contour serves structural purpose.
physical_description.dimensions: 14 cm length, 8 cm diameter (cylindrical); approximately 2 cm diameter pressure vent ports on opposite ends
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty for its size—feels dense and substantive in the palm, suggesting carefully distributed mass. Not unwieldy, but demands respect from the handler due to its center-of-gravity concentration.
physical_description.primary_material: Ceramic-alloy composite shell with reinforced steel pressure rings at equator and end caps
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with a faint iridescent sheen where the ceramic-alloy catches light. Deliberately unreflective. Light surface scoring and micro-cracks visible on close inspection—intentional roughness for grip integrity and visual authenticity of 'used industrial equipment.'
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate gray primary with charcoal pressure-containment bands. Accent: pale phosphorescent warning striping (3mm) running the length in compliance with Tier 3+ handling regulations
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare ceramic-alloy with subtle crosshatch etching for non-slip handling. Cool to touch, slightly porous to fingertip.
distinctive_features: Pressurized bulge at center—visible swelling suggests internal hydrolytic suspension
Two opposing vented ports (0.8 cm diameter) with microscopic crystalline residue around edges indicating chemical activity history
Faint geometric etching on casing: TESSERA CORPORATION corporate lattice pattern, subtle but unmistakable
Tri-color indicator lights (red/yellow/green) embedded in end cap—status indicators for charge integrity and trigger readiness
Small cylindrical protrusion on base: proprietary wireless detonation interface, sealed with wax-like compound
Hairline fracture pattern radiating from one pressure vent—cosmetic but suggests this is a field-worn unit, not factory fresh
Cryptic alphanumeric serial etched faintly: HDC-2-7734-SALTFLAT-CWF
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: COGNITIVE WELLNESS FOUNDATION in sans-serif block letters (0.5 cm height) stamped horizontally 3 cm from top end cap. Below it: smaller text reading 'TESSERA COMPONENT — NeutraFlush Compatible.' Logos are flush-stamped, intentionally matte to avoid reflection.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly deployed. No rust or corrosion (ceramic-alloy prevents this), but surface shows handling wear: minor scuff marks, one small dent on the cylindrical body suggesting rough transport. Indicator lights are bright and operational. Pressure seals show no weeping. This is a working weapon between operations, not a showpiece.
